controls.label: TypeScript. 8 years on the board. Daily. Strict mode, no any. Types are the first draft of the docs.
JavaScript. 8 years on the board. Daily. The platform underneath everything else, and still where the bugs live.
CSS. 8 years on the board. Daily. Grid, container queries and custom properties before any library.
GLSL. 4 years on the board. Weekly. Shaders for charts and the occasional hero that earns its place.
React. 8 years on the board. Daily. Server components where they help, plain state where they do not.
Next.js. 6 years on the board. Daily. The default for products that need a server and a deadline.
Astro. 3 years on the board. Weekly. For docs and content sites that should ship almost no JavaScript.
Svelte. 2 years on the board. Comfortable. Small tools and prototypes; I read it more often than I write it.
Vite. 5 years on the board. Daily. Fast feedback is a feature. Builds measured in seconds, not coffee.
Node.js. 7 years on the board. Weekly. Build scripts, small APIs and the glue between services.
Storybook. 6 years on the board. Weekly. Every component in isolation, with its states written down.
Figma. 7 years on the board. Weekly. I read design files fluently and push tokens back into them.
Playwright. 5 years on the board. Daily. End-to-end tests on the flows that make money, on every pull request.
Vitest. 4 years on the board. Daily. Unit tests that run before I have switched windows.
Testing Library. 6 years on the board. Weekly. Tests that use the interface the way a person does.
Lighthouse CI. 5 years on the board. Weekly. A performance budget the build enforces, so nobody has to argue.
